name: Rationalising with conjugates
whenToUse: A denominator contains a sum or difference of square roots, or a sum of such fractions looks like it could telescope.
pitfall: Multiply top AND bottom by the conjugate. The denominator becomes $a - b$, which may be negative, so watch the sign.
derivation: Multiply numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}$ and use the difference of squares $(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b})(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{b}) = a - b$.
